html:
A major earthquake in northern Iran just after midnight on 21 June 1990. It struck the provinces of Gilan and Zanjan near the Caspian Sea and killed between 35,000 and 50,000 people.

Its magnitude was 7.4. It hit at night, when most people were indoors, and flattened the towns of Rudbar and Manjil and hundreds of villages in the hills, where houses of mud brick and stone gave no protection. Landslides buried more. Hundreds of thousands were left homeless.

It came less than two years after the end of the Iran-Iraq War, and the country was poor and worn out. The Islamic Republic accepted foreign aid, including from countries it was hostile to, such as the United States. The disaster led Iran to bring in a stricter building code. The Bam earthquake of 2003 showed how much was still to be done.
sum: A major earthquake in northern Iran just after midnight on 21 June 1990. It struck the provinces of Gilan and Zanjan near the Caspian Sea and killed between 35,000 and 50,000 people.
